correctness.rationale: For every real 0<h<=1, the source vertex side lengths are 2,L,L, L=sqrt(1+h^2). Symmetrization imposes only a single unrestricted coefficient q at the fixed hypotenuse midpoint. Two explicit source 1-Lipschitz functions yield lower bound max(2L|q|/h, |L-2(L-1)q|), minimized exactly at q=Lh/(2[L+h(L-1)]) with value L^2/[L+h(L-1)]. An explicit positive operator using this q at the hypotenuse midpoint and ordinary pair averages at the other two midpoints satisfies all 15 target pairs: seven direct pairs contract, the two midpoint pairs contract, three pairs saturate the stated norm, and the remaining two opposite pairs are controlled by the strict comparison (sqrt(2)-1)/(2sqrt(2)-1)>2/9>=(4/[sqrt(L^2+8)(L+2+sqrt(L^2+8))]). Algebraic identities cover the entire interval and the right endpoint; no finite sample is treated as an infinite proof. The embedded Decimal checker independently inspects six extremal vertex potentials times 15 target pairs at 124 rational heights (11,160 comparisons), with equality witnesses and the classical rule comparison. All computations were executed successfully on their current actual file paths. The relative projection interpretation follows the finite-dimensional duality established by Basso (2021), Eq. (1.6).

originality.rationale: The searched closest complete statement is a formula for the fixed affine barycentric interpolation of triangles, not the infimum over all extensions to the vertices plus three midpoints. In the obtuse isosceles family, that fixed rule has norm L/h, strictly greater than the sharp new L^2/[L+h(L-1)] and unbounded as h tends to zero. The 2018 and 2021 primary sources provide existence, general extension/projection definitions, and optimization methodologies without computing these six-point constants. Other available results involving regular simplices, regular polygon midpoints, and rectangle midpoints have incompatible original vertex metric geometries. Actual meaning-based database queries and primary-text comparisons found no source whose mathematical conclusion implies the present parameter-family theorem. Remaining bibliographic incompleteness is recorded, so uniqueness is not asserted. This assessment is not an independent audit.

value.rationale: This is a sharp exact natural functional-analytic extension invariant on the entire similarity class of nondegenerate obtuse/right isosceles Euclidean triangles, not an arbitrary isolated sample. Simultaneous positive attainment at all three midpoints is nontrivial. In the flat-cell limit the best extension remains stable (lambda_h->1) even as ordinary affine midpoint interpolation has norm sqrt(1+h^2)/h->infinity. The explicit coefficient formula applies unchanged to arbitrary real Banach-valued inputs, producing a usable positive stability guarantee while scalar witnesses establish the sharp universal threshold. The distinction between unrestricted optimal interpolation and fixed barycentric interpolation is geometrically and analytically motivated. No downstream global mesh theorem is claimed.
